_policy: POST-CUTOVER BASELINE SEALING. Every successful cutover invalidates the tracked reference it
used, because R(L) == A can only hold while A describes current production.
A_next = R(L_post) is accepted for ONE reason: L_post matched the materialized target that
was just approved. Never because it is live, never because it is newer.
FAIL CLOSED: if the most recent record for a workflow is not SEALED, the next deployment of
that workflow is refused until it is.

sealProof.method: offline rebuild: applyDelta(delta(A,B), A), redacted, compared to R(L_current)

_note: SEALED 2026-08-27. Recorded UNSEALED first, because that was the truth: P7.5R deployed 45
nodes while the tracked reference was still the 33-node pre-Model-B export, so R(L) == A
could not hold and the next deployment failed closed rather than comparing against a
reference that described neither the old production nor the new one.
SEALING NEEDED A LIVE READ, but the acceptance test was offline-computable: R(L_pre) == A
held at the time, so the approved P7.5R target redacts to applyDelta(delta(A,B), A). The
fresh live read was required to equal that and did, with the version chain intact -- see
sealProof above and docs/P8_3A_P7_5R_BASELINE_SEAL.md. A proof, not a rubber stamp.
its versionId must equal preVersionId here, and the tracked reference postVersionId.
